steals.value: Make the price ladder explicit: fal.ai Rodin ($0.40), TRELLIS.2 ($0.25–$0.35), TRELLIS ($0.02) and TripoSR ($0.07) make it possible to sell a cheap proof before a premium final (https://fal.ai/models/fal-ai/hyper3d/rodin).
Copy Hyper3D's preview-before-confirming-credit-spend and free-start pattern; it reduces the risk of trying a one-photo product reconstruction (https://hyper3d.ai/pricing).
Copy 3D AI Studio's one-upload funnel, browser auto-rotate preview, eight-format export and customer-owned commercial assets (https://www.3daistudio.com/ImageTo3D).
Copy Alpha3D's continuation beyond generation: retopology, UV unwrap, PBR texturing and export in the same workflow (https://alpha3d.io/image-to-3d).
Copy Kaedim's customer-IP posture and human QA/revision loop for high-value equipment; it states full ownership/commercial rights and no training on customer IP (https://www.kaedim3d.com).
Copy TRELLIS's documented mesh-to-video sample path: render_video plus GLB export, then add a vertical aspect-ratio preset (https://github.com/microsoft/TRELLIS).
Use Poly Haven's CC0 HDRIs, textures and models for orbit-ad lighting/set dressing without a commercial asset fee (https://polyhaven.com/license).
Copy Needle's no-per-view-fee commercial hosting model for the interactive GLB review/QR upsell, while keeping the 9:16 MP4 as a separate deliverable (https://needle.tools/pricing).
Copy 8th Wall's free/no-login commercial AR distribution as an upsell: the same GLB can become an image-target WebAR experience (https://8thwall.org/).
Copy Zakeke's variant/configurator and dynamic-pricing framing for a second sale after the first orbit ad (https://www.zakeke.com/3d-configurator-for-ecommerce/).

do_not_copy.value: Do not treat a GLB as a finished ad: most candidates stop at mesh/AR/PDP output and do not state a ready-to-post 9:16 MP4 orbit. Budget a camera, render and vertical-crop step (https://trellis3d.co).

Do not sell TRELLIS.2 for commercial client work without resolving the license contradiction: GitHub describes MIT, while the project page says its materials are academic/research-only and not for commercial exploitation (https://microsoft.github.io/TRELLIS.2/).

Do not ignore license thresholds: Stable Fast 3D requires registration for commercial use, attribution/notice on distribution, and enterprise licensing above $1M annual revenue (https://huggingface.co/stabilityai/stable-fast-3d/blob/main/LICENSE.md).

Do not promise one-photo fidelity for products with hidden geometry; use multi-view when available and disclose that unseen sides are inferred. Hyper3D, Alpha3D and Kaedim all document optional/additional views for more control (https://hyper3d.ai/features/image-to-3d).
Do not copy Cylindo's four-photo requirement as a one-photo offer, or imply that its custom sales pricing is a per-generation price (https://www.cylindo.com).

Do not make Kaedim or Threekit the default same-week low-ticket path: both are demo/enterprise-oriented, and Kaedim says current off-the-shelf plans are temporarily closed or quote-led (https://docs.kaedim3d.com/welcome/faq).

Do not confuse delivery tools with reconstruction: Needle, Theatre.js and 8th Wall can host/animate/deliver a generated asset, but their fetched pages do not document one-photo-to-mesh generation (https://engine.needle.tools/docs/cloud/).
Do not source a random CGTrader model without checking the asset-specific license; the marketplace exposes royalty-free, editorial and custom license categories (https://www.cgtrader.com/).
